When you initially see something on the news, you only see the ending. It's easy to say, "well, that guy shouldn't have run from the police" - that's true (it's even true in this case) but it's also interesting to look deeper and find out why he ran.

Walter Scott had four children with two different women. But he had a decent job and he paid child support. He was getting by. But in 2003 there was a clerical error on the part of the state. "Checks he sent to a state agency for his ex-wife were mistakenly directed to the mother of his first children." As a result of this error (and remember, this was not his fault) he was sent to jail.

He lost his job, but not his child support obligations. This sent him into a cycle of falling behind, going to jail, and then losing whatever employment he had found.

On April 4th of this year, there was a warrant out for his arrest because he'd fallen behind again. And so, when he was pulled over for a broken taillight, he ran. The police officer shot and killed him - and that police officer has been charged with murder.

But now, as they say, you know the rest of the story. He wasn't a drug dealer or whatever. He just owed the state money. He was a man who felt trapped in an unfair system. What happened to him isn't only about police brutality. It's also an indictment of the way we treat fathers. Had he not run away, or not been killed, he'd be in jail right now only you wouldn't know his name. This MSN article interviews his brother and the last line is chilling.

He asked the judge, "How am I supposed to live?"

And the judge said something like, "That’s your problem. You figure it out."

I'm reminded of this (very long) interview with Dave Foley who you may remember as the actor in Kids in the Hall. When his show was cancelled, his child support payments continued. At the one hour mark he says that the judge told him:

Your ability to pay is not related to your obligation to pay

A very rich guy, and a very poor guy, both in the same crazy kafkaesque trap. It can happen to you too.
I guess the answer would be don't have children or if you do make sure the mother never knows your name. Sad really
